0.original: The next feat awaits, and Alphinaud would have you on the road as soon as possible.

24.original: Search for villagers of middle age and older.

27.original: Speak with Hunmu Rruk yet again.

48.original: Now, we must hasten to the next feat. Though I find myself a touch reluctant to do so, given Mablu's parting words...

49.original: One final feat remains. After this one, I hardly know what to expect.

50.original: Feat of the Brotherhood, here we come!

51.original: We need to start considering how to reclaim that keystone from Bakool Ja Ja...

52.original: Seeing as we now face the penultimate objective of the rite, it would be wise to travel to Mamook and undertake the Feat of the Brotherhood without delay.

53.original: Wise, yes, but impossible. The Ty'iinbek Traverse, which connects the upper forest to the Ja Tiika Heartland, is still impassable.

55.original: I'm afraid not. Work to clear the path is underway, though, so I'm hopeful we can resume our journey soon.

56.original: Then let us each use this time as we see fit.

57.original: I, for one, would like to explore the village's surrounds─if Erenville would oblige me with a tour?

58.original: Very well. I have no other engagements.

59.original: Then I will come with you─if only to prove that I <hex:021A020203>am<hex:021A020103> capable of keeping my footing.

60.original: Though I shouldn't rejoice in our delay, it does afford me an opportunity to look into my grandfather's purported visit to Yak T'el.

61.original: Oh, that's right! Mablu did say something about a foreign mage coming through here decades back, didn't she? I'll come with you!

63.original: Let us reconvene here after our respective diversions.

64.original: As I recall, the merchant met my grandfather at a market in Yak T'el some twenty years ago.

65.original: Any who might reliably remember him must therefore be at least middle-aged. Let us make inquiries where we can.

66.original: This fellow looks promising! Definitely older than I am.

67.original: I hope someone in Iq Br'aax knows something...

68.original: A foreign mage, twenty years ago?

69.original: Yes, I remember him. It's not often we get visitors from across the salt, let alone those traveling with infants. A baby girl, as I recall.

70.original: I only saw him in passing, mind─if anyone were to know more, I'd wager it would be Hunmu Rruk. He was already Xbr'aax Rax then.

71.original: A baby girl? It couldn't have been...

72.original: Th-Thank you, sir! That information is very helpful.

73.original: If you want to know more about that mage, I'd suggest speaking with Hunmu Rruk. He's sure to remember him.

74.original: So Hunmu Rruk has been Xbr'aax Rax for over twenty years... That's before I was even born!

75.original: This may be the very lead I was hoping for!

76.original: Hello again. Do you require assistance?

77.original: A foreign mage passed through Iq Br'aax roughly twenty years ago, possibly carrying a young child. Do you remember him?

78.original: Why do you ask me this? Who is this man to you?

79.original: He may have been my grandfather, and I wish to know what brought him here.

81.original: Not by blood, but he is family nonetheless.

82.original: A foreign mage did indeed visit Iq Br'aax. Master Galuf.

83.original: So far as his identity is concerned, I trust you are satisfied?

84.original: More than that, however, I cannot say.

86.original: I simply cannot. I beg your forgiveness and understanding.

87.original: Very well, I will not press. Thank you for confirming his presence here─the rest I will discover myself.

88.original: Out of more <hex:021A020203>general<hex:021A020103> curiosity, I have another question. They say the Yok Huy once dwelled in these forests. Where was that, exactly?

89.original: <hex:021A020203>General<hex:021A020103> curiosity, indeed... But yes. Before they withdrew to Urqopacha some five centuries ago, the Yok Huy claimed Yak T'el as their own.

90.original: Many of their architectural remains can be found in the lower forests─the Ja Tiika Heartland.

91.original: Then that's where they must have had their visions...

92.original: Thank you. That answers much and more.

93.original: I understand what it means to long for one's family. So believe me when I say that, though my position forbids me from aiding you further, I wish you nothing but success.

94.original: By helping the Third Promise find the golden city, you will surely find the answers to your questions.

95.original: Speaking of which, I have a query of my own for you, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>.

96.original: May I request a moment of your company?

97.original: Go on. We'll wait for you.

98.original: Go on and see what Hunmu Rruk needs.

99.original: So in order to get my answers, I need to find the golden city...

100.original: Well, that was my intent from the first. I'll do everything in my power to make it happen!

102.original: First, let us head to the cenote behind this village.

103.original: It was my intention to see you off without saying anything, but Mistress Krile's plea has softened my resolve...

104.original: As the leader of our community, I am gladdened to see that the Third Promise has surrounded herself with such compassionate and trustworthy companions.

105.original: Would you tell me of her journey thus far?

106.original: Is that so... It seems the rite has been a source of great learning and growth for Wuk Lamat.

107.original: It does me well to hear that.

108.original: ...My daughter would be about her age.

109.original: Girls are rarely born amongst the Xbr'aal. So when she arrived, the village was elated. Such joy I felt when first I held her...and pain when I found her at the bottom of a cenote.

110.original: Three years old. An accident, it was said. But I knew better.

112.original: Though we never caught them, a suspicious figure was seen fleeing towards the Ja Tiika Heartland. Towards Mamook.

113.original: Once bitter enemies, the Mamool Ja and Xbr'aal had learned to live in peace...

114.original: But who could doubt the intent of such a reprehensible act? By targeting the child who would one day lead her people, the criminal sought to undermine the future of the Xbr'aal.

115.original: I was determined not to let them succeed. And so I let the memory of my daughter die in that cenote, and gave her into the care of the one person I knew who could protect her.

117.original: Though she was born to lead the Xbr'aal, fate had a greater plan for Wuk Lamat.

118.original: Only the Dawnservant and I know the truth. But I must now take you into my confidence for one reason.

119.original: If the villain who attempted to murder my daughter was indeed of Mamook, then rancor towards the Xbr'aal still burns.

120.original: I was caught off guard once. I will not suffer the same tragedy again.

121.original: And so I ask you, not as the Dawnservant's elector but as a father, to watch over the Third Promise. Defend her from her enemies that may be lurking in shadow. Will you do this for me?

122.original: Thank you. From the bottom of my heart.

123.original: (-Vow of Resolve Gulool Ja Ja-)Will you hear my question and answer me plainly? Address me not as the ruler of Tuliyollal, but a concerned father.

124.original: Suffice it to say, this conversation must remain between us. Pray breathe not a word of this to anyone.
